Accordion.name: Accordion
Accordion.role: A vertical stack of collapsible panels that shows and hides sections of content.
usage: Break long content into sections the reader expands on demand (FAQ, documentation)
Reveal details progressively without crowding the initial view
Group settings or options by category
Present questions and answers in a compact format
Walk through a hierarchy of content
constraints: **MUST NOT** — hold critical content that has to stay visible at all times
**MUST NOT** — nest an `Accordion` inside another: one level only
**MUST** — give each trigger explicit text, never an icon alone
**Note** — a disabled trigger drops pointer events and applies `opacity-disabled`
**MUST NOT** — serve as primary navigation → use `NavigationMenu` or `Tabs`

anatomy.role: A single panel, with a bottom border
Button that opens and closes the panel
Caret showing whether the panel is open
Panel content, animated as it opens

props.description: Opening mode: one panel at a time, or several at once
Value of the panel(s) open on first render
Called when the open panel changes
Lets the reader close every panel (`single` mode)
Disables every trigger in the accordion

states.behavior: `ring-1 ring-ring/50` ring and `border-ring` border on the trigger
Panel open, caret pointing up, content sliding down

Accordion.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Accordion](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/) (Radix Accordion)

**Role**: Each trigger is a `button` inside a heading, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a `region` labelled by its trigger.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                     | Action                                             |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` / `Space`       | Opens or closes the focused trigger's panel        |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Next / previous trigger                            |
| `Home` / `End`          | First / last trigger                               |
| `Tab`                   | Leaves the triggers for the next focusable content |

**Accessible name**: The `AccordionTrigger` text names the button and labels the panel: it must describe the content, not say "See more".

**Pitfalls**:

- Do not put an interactive element inside `AccordionTrigger`: a button cannot contain another one.
- The heading level that wraps the trigger must fit the page's heading hierarchy.

Alert.name: Alert
Alert.role: A non-modal banner that delivers a contextual message — informational or an error — with a title, a description and an optional action.
usage: Report an authentication error after a failed sign-in
Tell the user about a system state (session expired, network error)
Warn before an irreversible action
Put an SVG icon first to strengthen the visual signal
constraints: **MUST NOT** — show a transient message (toast) → use `Sonner`
**MUST NOT** — act as a blocking dialog → use `AlertDialog`
**MUST NOT** — place more than one `Alert` per page section
**MUST NOT** — add a second `role="alert"` among the children: the root already carries it
**MUST NOT** — put variable-width content in `AlertAction`, which is absolutely positioned at the top right
dependencies: An SVG icon (Phosphor Icons) — a direct child of `Alert`, which switches the layout to two columns

anatomy.role: Bold title `<div>`; moves to `col-start-2` when an icon is present
Action `<div>`, absolutely positioned at the top right
First `<svg>` child: spans 2 grid rows, sized `size-4`

states.behavior: `text-destructive` text, description at `text-destructive/90`; the icon inherits the current color
Not applicable (the component is not interactive)

Alert.accessibility:
**Pattern**: `alert` role (assertive live region)

**Role**: `role="alert"` on the root: screen readers announce the content as soon as it is inserted.

**Keyboard**:

No keyboard interaction of its own; only the interactive elements placed inside receive focus.

**Accessible name**: The title (`AlertTitle`) and the description (`AlertDescription`) make up the announced message.

**Pitfalls**:

- `role="alert"` interrupts whatever is being read: keep `Alert` for important messages that appear in response to the user, not for a static notice present on page load.
- The `destructive` variant does not carry the meaning on its own: the text must say it is an error (icon plus words, never color alone).

AlertDialog.name: AlertDialog
AlertDialog.role: A blocking modal that stops the user to confirm or cancel a critical action.
usage: Confirm an irreversible action (deletion, cancellation, final submission)
Ask for explicit approval before a destructive change
Show a warning the user has to answer
Block the rest of the interface until the user has made a choice

**Choice** (`rule-21`) — Pick the surface from how much it blocks and how long its content is. A blocking decision (confirm, destroy): `AlertDialog`. A short task with no inner scrolling: `Dialog`. Long content or side context: `Sheet` from `md` up, `Drawer` below — **unless** it is side navigation, which stays a `Sheet` at every width (this is what `Sidebar` does below `md`). Anchored, non-blocking content with no scrolling and at most 3 fields: `Popover`. An informative preview on hover, from `md` up: `HoverCard`. A one-line, non-interactive label of at most 80 characters: `Tooltip`.
constraints: **MUST NOT** — carry a plain informational message → use `Dialog`, or `Sonner` for a notification
**MUST NOT** — open an `AlertDialog` on top of another: one visible at a time
**MUST** — offer a cancel button (`AlertDialogCancel`)
**MUST NOT** — re-implement the focus trap: Radix provides it
**MUST** — render an `AlertDialogTitle`: it is the name screen readers announce
dependencies: `AlertDialog` from `radix-ui` (Root, Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, Title, Description, Action, Cancel)

anatomy.role: Portal that renders outside the parent DOM
Optional media or icon area in the header

props.description: Whether the dialog is open (controlled mode)
Called when the dialog opens or closes
`sm` keeps the box narrow and its content centered at every width; `default` widens it and left-aligns the header from the `sm` breakpoint up

states.behavior: Overlay shown, content centered, animated with `fade-in` and `zoom-in-95`
Focus trapped inside the dialog (Radix focus trap)
The Action and Cancel buttons can each be disabled with `disabled`

AlertDialog.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Alert Dialog](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/) (Radix AlertDialog)

**Role**: `role="alertdialog"`; labelled by `AlertDialogTitle`, described by `AlertDialogDescription`. Modal: while it is open, the rest of the page is `aria-hidden` (Radix sets no `aria-modal`).

**Keyboard**:

| Key                 | Action                                                      |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the focusable elements, trapped in the dialog |
| `Escape`            | Closes the dialog (same as Cancel)                          |
| `Enter` / `Space`   | Activates the focused button                                |

**Accessible name**: `AlertDialogTitle` is required; `AlertDialogDescription` must state what the action will do.

**Pitfalls**:

- On open, focus goes to `AlertDialogCancel`: the destructive action must never be the default choice.
- On close, focus returns to the trigger.
- Clicking outside does not close the dialog. That is deliberate: the decision must be explicit.
AlertDialog.code_example:
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/alert-dialog"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="destructive">Delete</Button>
      </AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this item?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>
            This cannot be undone. The data will be permanently deleted.
          </AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
          <AlertDialogAction variant="destructive">Delete</AlertDialogAction>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  )
}

AspectRatio.name: AspectRatio
AspectRatio.role: A container that locks its content — an image, a video, an embedded map — to a fixed width-to-height ratio.
usage: Show an image or a video at a constant ratio (16/9, 4/3, 1/1…)
Keep a grid of thumbnails visually consistent
Frame embedded content (an iframe, a map) without shifting the layout
Reserve a media element's space before it loads, so it does not push the layout around (_cumulative layout shift_)
constraints: **MUST NOT** — hold free-flowing text: it would be clipped or overflow
**MUST** — fill the frame with an `absolute` child (`size-full`) or an `object-cover` media element
**MUST** — pass a single direct child; wrap several elements in a container

states.behavior: The container renders at the given ratio

AspectRatio.accessibility:
**Pattern**: None — a layout container

**Role**: No role: a `div` that sets its child's ratio.

**Keyboard**:

No keyboard interaction.

**Accessible name**: Carried by the content: a child image has its `alt` (empty when decorative), a video its captions.

**Pitfalls**:

- Cropping must not hide information the image exists to convey.

Avatar.name: Avatar
Avatar.role: A visual stand-in for a person or an entity — a photo, initials or an icon — with support for groups and status badges.
usage: Show a user's profile photo in a header or a list
Fall back to initials when the image is unavailable
Stack several avatars with `AvatarGroup` to list participants
Signal a status (online, notifications) with `AvatarBadge`
Size it to the context (`sm` in lists, `lg` on profiles)
constraints: **MUST** — provide an `AvatarFallback`, shown when the image is missing
**MUST NOT** — use `AvatarBadge` without an `aria-label` that says what it signals
**MUST** — give `AvatarImage` a descriptive `alt`
**MUST NOT** — show more than 4 avatars in an `AvatarGroup`: beyond that, show the first 3 and put the rest in `AvatarGroupCount`

anatomy.role: Status badge, positioned at the bottom right
Count of the extra avatars in a group

states.behavior: Avatar shown with its image or fallback, at `size-8`
The image has loaded; the fallback is hidden
The image failed; the fallback (initials) is shown
Not applicable directly (left to interactive parents)

Avatar.accessibility:
**Pattern**: Image (`img`) with a text fallback (Radix Avatar)

**Role**: `AvatarImage` renders an `img`; `AvatarFallback` only shows when the image fails or is missing.

**Keyboard**:

No keyboard interaction of its own.

**Accessible name**: `alt` is required on `AvatarImage` (the person's name), or `alt=""` when the name is already written next to it.

**Pitfalls**:

- When the name is shown next to the avatar, the fallback initials repeat it: hide them with `aria-hidden`.
- A clickable avatar must be wrapped in a named link or button, not made clickable itself.
Avatar.code_example:
import {
  Avatar,
  AvatarImage,
  AvatarFallback,
  AvatarBadge,
  AvatarGroup,
  AvatarGroupCount,
} from "@/components/ui/avatar"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <AvatarGroup>
      <Avatar size="default">
        <AvatarImage src="/user1.jpg" alt="Sarah Miller" />
        <AvatarFallback>SM</AvatarFallback>
        <AvatarBadge />
      </Avatar>
      <Avatar size="default">
        <AvatarImage src="/user2.jpg" alt="James Carter" />
        <AvatarFallback>JC</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
      <AvatarGroupCount>+3</AvatarGroupCount>
    </AvatarGroup>
  )
}

Badge.name: Badge
Badge.role: A compact label that categorizes an element, marks its status or highlights a piece of metadata.
usage: Show a status (active, pending, error) next to a title
Categorize an entry in a list or a table
Display a notification count
Flag something new or experimental
Wrap a link with `asChild` to make the badge clickable
constraints: **MUST NOT** — act as an action button → use `Button` with `size="xs"`
**MUST NOT** — exceed three words of text
**MUST** — keep the `destructive` variant for error or critical-alert statuses
**MUST NOT** — contain an interactive element
**MUST** — check the contrast of the background-less `ghost` and `link` variants on every surface they appear on

exports.name: badgeVariants
exports.summary: A `cva` function: returns the classes for a combination of its axes (see **Variants**), to give another element this style.

props.description: Renders the first child instead, through Radix Slot

states.behavior: Background opacity shifts, depending on the variant (links and ghost)

Badge.accessibility:
**Pattern**: Static text (`span`); a link when rendered with `asChild`

**Role**: No role of its own; takes on the role of the element passed through `asChild` (an `a`, for example).

**Keyboard**:

No keyboard interaction of its own; a badge rendered as a link behaves like a native link (`Enter`).

**Accessible name**: The badge text. A badge that holds only an icon needs `sr-only` text.

**Pitfalls**:

- Color never carries the meaning on its own (`destructive` says "Error" in words, it is not just red).
- A count ("3") must be tied to what it counts — in the name of the neighboring button, for example.

Breadcrumb.name: Breadcrumb
Breadcrumb.role: Secondary navigation that shows the path to the current page, so the user can climb back up the hierarchy.
usage: Show the trail on pages two or more levels deep
Let the user jump back to a parent page
Show where the user stands in the site's hierarchy
Collapse long paths behind an ellipsis in deep hierarchies
constraints: **MUST NOT** — serve as primary navigation: it is a contextual landmark
**MUST** — place a single `Breadcrumb` per page, at the top of the main content
**MUST NOT** — make the last item (`BreadcrumbPage`) clickable
**Note** — separators and the ellipsis are hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`)
**MUST NOT** — replace the root's `aria-label="breadcrumb"`, **unless** to translate it
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the `UI_STRINGS.breadcrumb` strings (`srLabel` on `BreadcrumbEllipsis`)

anatomy.role: Ordered list `<ol>` that holds the items
Clickable link to a parent page
Visual separator between items (a right caret by default)
Marks where a long path has been collapsed

props.description: Additional CSS classes on the root `<nav>`
Renders the first child instead, passing it the props and classes (Radix `Slot`)
Text read by screen readers; overrides the `UI_STRINGS` value

states.behavior: The browser's native focus style on links (no custom ring)
Not applicable — links go to their target page

Breadcrumb.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Breadcrumb](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/)

**Role**: A `nav` labelled `UI_STRINGS.breadcrumb.landmark` that holds an `ol`; `BreadcrumbPage` carries `aria-current="page"`.

**Keyboard**:

No interaction of its own: links behave natively (`Tab`, `Enter`).

**Accessible name**: The `nav` landmark is named "breadcrumb" by default; translate it through the prop provided. The ellipsis announces `UI_STRINGS.breadcrumb.ellipsis`.

**Pitfalls**:

- Separators are hidden (`role="presentation"`, `aria-hidden`): never put meaningful text in them.
- The current page is not a link: do not make it clickable.
Breadcrumb.code_example:
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
  BreadcrumbPage,
} from "@/components/ui/breadcrumb"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/products">Products</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>Product details</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  )
}

Button.name: Button
Button.role: Triggers a primary or secondary action; comes in several visual variants and sizes.
usage: Submit a form (`type="submit"`)
Trigger a key action (for example "Sign in", "Confirm")
Navigate within the app through `asChild` and `<Link>`
Icon-only actions (the `icon-*` sizes)
Destructive button for irreversible actions (the `destructive` variant)
constraints: **MUST NOT** — render a `<button>` to navigate to an external site → an `<a href>`, through `asChild` to keep the look
**MUST NOT** — place more than 2 `variant="default"` (primary) buttons in the same view
**MUST NOT** — convey a state through color alone: add text or a tooltip
**MUST** — give an `icon-*` button an `aria-label`
**MUST NOT** — nest a `<button>` inside another, including through `asChild`

exports.name: buttonVariants
exports.summary: A `cva` function: returns the classes for a combination of its axes (see **Variants**), to give another element this style.

props.description: Renders the first child instead, through Radix Slot

states.behavior: Background dims slightly (90 % opacity), depending on the variant
Shifts down by `translate-y-px` as tactile feedback (except with `aria-haspopup`)
Render a `<Spinner>` as a child; the consumer sets `aria-busy="true"`

Button.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/) — native `button` element

**Role**: Native `button` (or the element passed through `asChild`, such as a link).

**Keyboard**:

| Key               | Action                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activates the button            |
| `Tab`             | Moves focus to the next element |

**Accessible name**: The button text. The `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm` and `icon-lg` sizes have no visible text: `aria-label` is required.

**Pitfalls**:

- **MUST** — when the user needs to understand why the action is unavailable, use `aria-disabled` and an explanation: `disabled` removes the button from the tab order.
- A button that navigates must be a link (`asChild` with an `a`), not an `onClick` that changes the page.
- `variant="destructive"` must come with an explicit label.

ButtonGroup.name: ButtonGroup
ButtonGroup.role: A container that visually joins adjacent buttons, inputs or selects by merging their borders and corners.
usage: Group related actions (for example "Previous / Next")
Join an input and an action button (a search field with a "Go" button)
Combine a select and a button in a compact toolbar
Stack buttons in a column with the `vertical` orientation
Split sub-groups visually with `ButtonGroupSeparator`
constraints: **MUST NOT** — group unrelated actions → just space them out (`flex gap-*`)
**MUST NOT** — group more than 5 buttons
**MUST** — keep `orientation="vertical"` for side toolbars
**MUST** — only hold children whose borders can merge: the inner corners are removed
**Note** — a nested group (`has-[>[data-slot=button-group]]`) automatically gets `gap-2`

anatomy.role: Visual separator between the group's items

exports.name: buttonGroupVariants
exports.summary: A `cva` function: returns the classes for a combination of its axes (see **Variants**), to give another element this style.

props.description: Direction the children are stacked in
Renders the first child instead, through Radix Slot

states.behavior: Horizontal group, merged borders, rounded ends
Stacked vertically; top and bottom borders merge
The focused child moves to `z-dropdown` so its focus ring shows above its neighbors
Left to the child components (Button, Select…)

ButtonGroup.accessibility:
**Pattern**: Group (`role="group"`)

**Role**: `role="group"` on the root; each button keeps its own semantics.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                 | Action                                                      |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves from one button to the next (no arrow-key navigation) |

**Accessible name**: Give the group an `aria-label` when its purpose is not obvious ("Text formatting").

**Pitfalls**:

- For an exclusive choice between options, use `ToggleGroup`, which carries the selected state; `ButtonGroup` only groups things visually.

Calendar.name: Calendar
Calendar.role: An interactive date picker built on `react-day-picker`: single, multiple or range selection, with month-by-month navigation.
usage: Pick a single date in a form (a date of birth, a due date)
Pick a date range (a billing period, time off)
Show a calendar in a `Popover` for date-picker fields
Navigate by month and year through the built-in dropdowns
Show week numbers where the business context calls for them (`showWeekNumber`)
constraints: **MUST NOT** — serve as a scheduler or planner (day or week views): the design system does not provide one
**MUST NOT** — show more than one `Calendar` per view, **unless** comparing two date ranges
**MUST** — place the `Calendar` inside a container (`Popover`, `Card`…): it does not position itself
**MUST** — keep disabled days visible (`opacity-disabled`, `aria-disabled`)
**MUST NOT** — break keyboard navigation (arrows between days, Tab to the controls)
dependencies: `react-day-picker` — the calendar engine and its types (`DayPicker`, `DayButton`, `Locale`)

props.description: How the caption is shown (a static label or dropdowns)
Shows the days of the previous and next months
Visual variant of the navigation buttons
Additional CSS classes on the container
Locale used to format dates and months

states.behavior: Day grid shown, no day selected
Hovered day with a dimmed background (through the `Button`'s `ghost` variant)
Visible focus ring (`ring-ring/50`, `border-ring`) on the focused day
Day cannot be selected: `opacity-disabled` and `aria-disabled`, `muted-foreground` text

Calendar.accessibility:
**Pattern**: A date [grid](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/) (react-day-picker)

**Role**: A grid of dates; the selected day carries `aria-selected`, unavailable days `aria-disabled`.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                               | Action                            |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight`        | Previous / next day               |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`           | Same day the previous / next week |
| `Home` / `End`                    | Start / end of the week           |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown`             | Previous / next month             |
| `Shift+PageUp` / `Shift+PageDown` | Previous / next year              |
| `Enter` / `Space`                 | Selects the focused day           |

**Accessible name**: react-day-picker names the month navigation buttons, in English by default: pass localized labels through its `labels` prop.

**Pitfalls**:

- A calendar alone is not enough to enter a date the user already knows: offer a text input as well.
- Mark unavailable days by something other than color.

Card.name: Card
Card.role: A surface that brings a title, a description, content and a footer together in one consistent structure.
usage: Wrap the sign-in form in a bounded surface
Present an entity (a profile, a setting, a notification) with its actions
Group mixed information visually on a dashboard
Use `data-size="sm"` for compact cards in dense lists

**Choice** (`rule-22`) — Pick how to present a collection from the nature of its content. Short-lived actions opened from a trigger: `DropdownMenuItem`. Rows to compare that share the same attributes, 3 or more per row: `Table`. A vertical list of entries (media, title, description, actions): `Item` inside an `ItemGroup`. A self-contained block with a header, body and footer, alone or in a grid: `Card`.
constraints: **MUST NOT** — nest `Card`s more than one level deep: show hierarchy with a different background
**MUST NOT** — put long content in `CardAction`, which sits at the top right of the header
**MUST NOT** — place more than 2 actions in `CardFooter`
**MUST NOT** — put `onClick` on a `Card`: wrap it in an `<a>` or a `<button>` when it is clickable

anatomy.role: Grid header that holds the title, description and action
Description or subtitle in a subdued color
Action area at the top right of the header
Footer with a top border, laid out horizontally

props.description: Card size: `gap-4 py-4` or `gap-2 py-3`. Rendered as `data-size` on the root

states.behavior: No dedicated style (a Card is not interactive by default)
Handle it with a skeleton inside `CardContent`

Card.accessibility:
**Pattern**: None — a layout container

**Role**: No role: plain `div`s. `CardTitle` is not a heading element.

**Keyboard**:

No keyboard interaction of its own.

**Accessible name**: Not applicable. When the card is a section of the page, wrap its title in a heading of the right level (`Heading`).

**Pitfalls**:

- A fully clickable card must contain a real link (whose hit area can be stretched), not an `onClick` on the container.
- `CardTitle` is a `div`, so it does not appear in a screen reader's list of headings.

Show a carousel of promotional or informational content
Step through visual stages or content previews
Feature items in a tight space with previous / next navigation
Scroll vertically through stacked content

**MUST NOT** — show more than one `Carousel` per view: their keyboard navigation conflicts
**MUST NOT** — hide the previous and next buttons
**MUST** — give the container a descriptive `aria-label`
**MUST** — contain a `CarouselContent` and at least one `CarouselItem`
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the `UI_STRINGS.carousel` strings (`srLabel` on `CarouselPrevious` and `CarouselNext`)

Button that goes to the previous slide
Button that goes to the next slide

Text read by screen readers; overrides the `UI_STRINGS` value

The current slide is visible in the carousel's viewport

Carousel.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Carousel](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) (Embla)

**Role**: `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`; each slide is a `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="slide"`.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                        | Action                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Previous / next slide, while focus is inside the carousel   |
| `Tab`                      | Reaches the previous / next buttons and the slides' content |

**Accessible name**: The previous / next buttons are named by `UI_STRINGS.carousel.previous` / `.next`. Give the carousel itself an `aria-label` ("Similar products").

**Pitfalls**:

- No auto-rotation without a pause button: content that moves on its own for more than 5 s must be stoppable (WCAG 2.2.2).
- The content of off-screen slides stays reachable from the keyboard: make sure the tab order still makes sense.

Chart.name: Chart
Chart.role: A container and a set of helpers for data visualization, built on `recharts`: theming, tooltips and a legend, all configured through a `ChartConfig` object.
usage: Draw bar, line, area or pie charts from structured data
Show a contextual tooltip when hovering a data point
Show a legend that describes the data series
Apply the theme's colors (light / dark) to the series automatically through `ChartConfig`

- The label must not change with the state: `aria-pressed` carries the state.

ToggleGroup.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Radio Group](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/) (`type="single"`) or a group of toggle buttons (`type="multiple"`) — Radix ToggleGroup

**Role**: `role="group"`; in `single` mode, each item carries `role="radio"` and `aria-checked`; in `multiple` mode, `aria-pressed`.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                                                     | Action                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`                                                   | Enters the group (a single tab stop) |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` (or `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`) | Next / previous item                 |
| `Home` / `End`                                          | First / last item                    |
| `Enter` / `Space`                                       | Turns the item on or off             |

**Accessible name**: Name the group (`aria-label`: "Text alignment"); every icon-only item needs an `aria-label`.

**Pitfalls**:

- For an exclusive choice presented as buttons, `type="single"` gives the expected radio semantics.

import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/ui/toggle-group"
import { ListIcon, GridIcon, TableIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react"

export default function Example() {

      type="single"
      defaultValue="list"
      variant="outline"
      size="default"
      aria-label="View"
    >
      <ToggleGroupItem value="list" aria-label="List view">
        <ListIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="grid" aria-label="Grid view">
        <GridIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="table" aria-label="Table view">
        <TableIcon />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  )
}

Tooltip.name: Tooltip
Tooltip.role: A small contextual label that appears when a trigger is hovered or focused, built on Radix Tooltip.
usage: Describe what an icon button with no visible label does
Show the keyboard shortcut of an action (with a nested `Kbd`)
Explain what an icon or an abbreviation means
Add a short complement of information to an interactive element
Show a short preview when hovering a link or a truncated element

**Choice** (`rule-21`) — Pick the surface from how much it blocks and how long its content is. A blocking decision (confirm, destroy): `AlertDialog`. A short task with no inner scrolling: `Dialog`. Long content or side context: `Sheet` from `md` up, `Drawer` below — **unless** it is side navigation, which stays a `Sheet` at every width (this is what `Sidebar` does below `md`). Anchored, non-blocking content with no scrolling and at most 3 fields: `Popover`. An informative preview on hover, from `md` up: `HoverCard`. A one-line, non-interactive label of at most 80 characters: `Tooltip`.
constraints: **MUST NOT** — contain interactive elements (links, buttons) → use `Popover`
**MUST NOT** — exceed one line or 80 characters of text
**MUST NOT** — be the only place critical information appears
**MUST** — place a `TooltipProvider` higher in the tree, for example in the root layout
**MUST NOT** — sit directly on a `disabled` element, which receives neither focus nor hover: wrap the element in a `<span tabIndex={0}>` that carries the trigger
dependencies: `radix-ui` — the `Tooltip` primitive (Provider, Root, Trigger, Content, Portal, Arrow)

anatomy.role: Logical root of the tooltip (opening and closing)
Content of the tooltip, rendered in a `Portal`

states.behavior: Appears after the configured delay (`fade-in` and `zoom-in-95` animation)
Same behavior as hover, triggered by keyboard navigation
Not applicable — the trigger must not be disabled

Tooltip.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Tooltip](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/) (Radix Tooltip)

**Role**: `role="tooltip"`; the tooltip describes the trigger (`aria-describedby`).

**Keyboard**:

| Key                  | Action            |
| -------------------- | ----------------- |
| Focus on the trigger | Shows the tooltip |
| `Escape`             | Hides it          |

**Accessible name**: A tooltip describes; it does not name: an icon-only button keeps its `aria-label` even with a tooltip.

**Pitfalls**:

- No essential information and no interactive content in a tooltip.
- A `disabled` button does not receive focus: its tooltip is out of keyboard reach.
- The content must stay visible while the pointer is over the tooltip itself (WCAG 1.4.13): do not shorten the delays.
Tooltip.code_example:
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/tooltip"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { Kbd } from "@/components/ui/kbd"
import { CopyIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger asChild>
          <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Copy">
            <CopyIcon />
          </Button>
        </TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent>
          Copy <Kbd>⌘C</Kbd>
        </TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  )
}
